title: Google SynthID Detector herkesin kullanımına açıldı
summary: Google, farklı yapay zeka araçlarıyla üretilen görsellerin, videoların ve ses dosyalarının tespit edilmesini sağlayan SynthID Detector aracını küresel çapta herkesin erişimine açtı.
body:
Google'ın duyurusuna göre, yapay zeka içeriklerini tespit etmeyi amaçlayan SynthID Detector aracı artık dünya genelinde tüm kullanıcıların erişimine sunuldu. Daha önce yalnızca sınırlı sayıda test kullanıcına ve medya profesyoneline açık olan sistem, synthid.com adresi üzerinden kullanılabiliyor.

## Hangi platformları destekliyor?

TechCrunch'ın aktardığına göre yeni web sitesi; görseller, videolar ve ses dosyaları için pek çok yaygın formatı destekliyor. Kullanıcılar yükledikleri dosyaların yapay zeka tarafından üretilip üretilmediğini bu araçla kontrol edebiliyor. Sistem bugüne kadar Google araçlarının yanı sıra OpenAI, NVIDIA ve Kakao tarafından oluşturulan filigranları tespit edebiliyor; Apple desteğinin ise yakında ekleneceği belirtiliyor.

## Nasıl kullanılıyor ve detaylar neler?

Android Authority'nin haberine göre, platformu kullanmak isteyenlerin Google, Apple veya OpenAI hesaplarından biriyle oturum açması gerekiyor. Google DeepMind verilerine göre şirket, 2023'ten bu yana 180 milyardan fazla görsel ve videonun yanı sıra binlerce saatlik ses içeriğine görünmez filigran ekledi. Öte yandan Google Arama, Gemini uygulaması ve Chrome'daki yerleşik doğrulama özelliklerinin günlük 1 milyon isteği aştığı ifade ediliyor.

**Neden önemli?** İnternetteki yapay zeka içeriklerinin artmasıyla birlikte, kullanıcıların karşılaştıkları medya dosyalarının kaynağını doğrulayabilmesi güvenilir bilgi için önem taşıyor.

source_texts.title: We're making it easier to identify AI-generated content globally.
source_texts.summary: We’re launching a standalone platform to help you easily identify whether online content was created using Google AI or tools from our industry partners.
source_texts.text:
We're making it easier to identify AI-generated content globally.
As AI tools become better and easier to use, having clear context about the content you encounter online helps you make informed decisions about what to trust. Since launching Google SynthID in 2023, we've helped people identify AI-generated media using imperceptible watermarks across images, video, and audio. To date, we've watermarked over 180 billion images and videos, along with 240,000 years of audio content.
Last year, we introduced an early version of the SynthID Detector to help media professionals verify AI-generated content. Now, we’re expanding access to everyone – with the tool available globally in English starting today.
With the new SynthID Detector, anyone can easily check if an image, video, or audio file was made with AI from Google or our partners, including OpenAI, NVIDIA, Kakao, and soon, Apple.
This tool joins our built-in verification features in Search, the Gemini app, and Chrome, which now regularly handle over 1 million requests daily. It’s all part of our ongoing work to give you more context about the media you see online, so you can navigate the web with confidence.

source_texts.title: Google’s cross-model AI detection tool is finally available for all
source_texts.summary: Synthid.com can detect AI watermarks from Google, OpenAI, Kakao, and more, and it's finally available for all to use.
source_texts.text:
Google's cross-model AI detection tool is finally available for all
Oct 7, 2026 — 10:00 AM ET
- Google has announced that the SynthID Detector portal is now available to all users globally, following a limited release.
- The portal, accessible at synthid.com, lets you check if a photo, video, or audio track was generated by AI.
- The SynthID Detector portal can detect watermarks made by Google, OpenAI, NVIDIA, and Kakao services, with Apple support coming soon.
Google and OpenAI have long allowed users to check media for SynthID watermarks. The presence of these watermarks almost guarantees that a media file was generated by AI. However, one major downside is that you need to use Gemini or OpenAI’s website to verify content. Google also has a dedicated SynthID Detector tool, but this has been limited to select testers for over a year now. Thankfully, that’s changing today.
Google has announced that the SynthID Detector portal (accessible at synthid.com) is now available to all users globally, allowing them to check whether a picture, video, or audio file was created or edited with AI. Furthermore, Google says this portal can detect SynthID watermarks created by itself, OpenAI, NVIDIA, Kakao, and “soon” Apple. That’s a welcome change from initial SynthID detection tools. For example, Gemini can only detect watermarks made with Google AI tools, while OpenAI’s verification website can only detect SynthID signatures made with OpenAI tools.
The company previously said that SynthID Detector goes a step further by highlighting specific parts of an image or video that have the SynthID watermark.
Anyone can log onto synthid.com using their Google, Apple, or OpenAI account to scan uploaded media files. I really hope the platform eventually offers the ability to sign in via an email account, though. After all, tech companies should be making it as easy as possible to check for AI-generated files. Right now, you’re out of luck if you want to verify a file without a Big Tech account.
We asked a Google representative about alternative login options and the possibility of authenticating files without logging in. However, they reiterated that you can only log in via a Google, Apple, or OpenAI account.
Nevertheless, this is a big step forward for media verification in the age of generative AI. This news also comes shortly after Anthropic announced that Claude can now add watermarks to AI-generated text. So our fingers are crossed for more AI services to embrace this verification tech.

source_texts.title: Google’s new SynthID website can identify AI-generated media
source_texts.summary: Google on Tuesday launched a new site that lets anyone verify whether a piece of media, be it an image, a video or an audio clip, is generated using AI.
source_texts.text:
Google on Tuesday launched a new site that lets anyone verify whether a piece of media, be it an image, a video or an audio clip, is generated using AI.
The company had made this tool available to select journalists, media professionals and researchers for testing at Google I/O last year, and is now opening up access to the tool to everyone.
The site supports JPG, JPEG, PNG, BMP, WEBP, AVIF, HEIC, HEIF, TIFF, TIF, and GIF formats for images; MP4, MOV, and WEBM for videos; and WAV, MP3, OGG, FLAC, AAC, and M4A for audio.
Google is using SynthID, which it introduced in 2023, to identify whether media is AI-generated. The company’s Nano Banana, Veo and Lyria models, as well as tools with generation capabilities, like Gemini, Flow, ProducerAI and Vids, all use SynthID to watermark any media they generate.
OpenAI, NVIDIA and Kakao also support SynthID, and OpenAI maintains its own site for checking content. Apple is said to be adding support soon, too.
Google has baked SynthID verification into the Gemini app and Google Chrome. The company said people currently make 1 million requests to verify content every day.
Microsoft and Meta have their own standards for watermarking and verifying content. However, these tools are not infallible, often failing to identify content created by their makers’ models.
